blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — For some vendors outside the Manila South Cemetery, selling flowers for the departed during Undas has been part of their livelihood for years already. And despite problems with the economy, for them, this year’s profit is enough to make ends meet. With arranged flowers lined up in the sidewalk, Bryan Amoyan is ready to pack his products once the gate of the cemetery closes at 9 p.m. The 40-year-old vendor told the INQUIRER that they have been selling flowers since October 29, Thursday.
